audience.programmeDescription: Arts and Culture Studies at Erasmus University Rotterdam examines how arts and creative industries work in society. It combines cultural sociology, economics, management, media and heritage with research methods. Students develop a focus area, complete an arts-and-culture internship and undertake an individual graduation project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The three UCR programmes offer different combinations of relevant fields. Matches show important shared content rather than course equivalence; blank cells preserve substantive differences. None of these programmes is an arts-and-health pathway. UCR’s general sociology and organisational study do not reproduce IBACS’s specialist cultural-sector curriculum or mandatory placement.

curriculum.routeLabel: Culture and Economics focus; minor pathway

componentNotes.minor: 15 EC of approved minor study, taken from the third year.
componentNotes.internship: Compulsory 15-EC arts-and-culture internship; entry requires completion of the first year.
componentNotes.graduation: Compulsory 15-EC individual graduation project; entry requires the first year and 45 EC from years two and three.

cellNotes.text: General organisational behaviour and leadership; partial overlap with cultural-sector management.
General sociological foundations; IBACS applies sociology specifically to arts and culture.
Primarily film history, form and interpretation, with a shorter introduction to wider media.

concepts.label: Arts, culture, economy & society
concepts.concept: Art history, heritage and literature connect with media, sociology, economics and organisations. Research methods support the study of cultural works, markets and social contexts; these general disciplines complement the arts without reproducing IBACS’s specialist cultural-sector sequence.

concepts.label: Culture, society & public life
concepts.concept: Art, heritage and history connect with sociology, law, philosophy and public policy to explore inequality, collective life and social conflict. Qualitative and quantitative methods support inquiry into culture’s place in public life; this is not an arts-and-health pathway.

concepts.label: Culture, media & digital society
concepts.concept: Film, media and literature connect with rhetoric, communication, audience research and digital change. Sociology and data methods support the study of representation, platforms and cultural participation; the programme does not provide a specialist cultural-sociology sequence.
